title: Adaptive Throttle Horizon — compact control panel for burst tuning
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and prototype a compact control panel for dedicated GPU pools that exposes an 'Adaptive Throttle Horizon' — a single, timeline-driven interface for tuning burst allowances, thermal headroom, and autoscale aggressiveness. Target users: SREs and capacity operators who need a quick surface for triage and short-term capacity tuning without opening the full policy editor. This ticket covers wireframes, an interactive Figma prototype, internal design review, and a first round of operator usability sessions. Key goals: reduce cognitive overhead for burst changes, make safe defaults obvious, and ensure that the UI communicates downstream effects (cost, SLO risk) before an operator applies a change.
design_notes: Primary affordance: a horizontal 'horizon' timeline (0-60m) showing current reserved capacity, predicted queue, and available burst budget
Knob controls: burst magnitude (percent of pool), duration presets (short/medium/long), and thermal headroom slider that ties to node-level throttling policies
Visual feedback: immediate cost delta and SLO risk band next to apply button; color coding for safe/warning/unsafe ranges
Fallbacks: changes are non-destructive by default (preview mode) and require explicit confirmation to persist to autoscale policy
Accessibility: keyboard and screen-reader labels for timeline markers and tooltips; focus order respects operator flows
Telemetry surface: small link to 'open in Telemetry' which pre-populates a Grafana query for the selected pool and horizon window
decisions: Use compact timeline rather than table of knobs to reduce clicks during incident triage — operators preferred a visual timeline in interviews
Preset durations (15m, 30m, 60m) plus custom slider chosen to balance speed and precision
Preview-only default: apply button opens a commit modal with an expected cost and SLO impact summary
Do not allow burst magnitude >25% of pool by default; require an admin opt-in label for higher limits
Integrate with rollouts: new burst settings will create a short-lived 'policy patch' that can be automatically rolled back if error rate increases beyond threshold
open_questions: How should we represent multi-queue pools where burst targets specific customer routes? (per-route vs pooled view)
What API contract will ENG provide for previewing cost and SLO impact; need a mock endpoint for prototype
Should thermal headroom be exposed to all operators or only to users with node-ops role?
Edge case: how to show conflicting scheduled autoscale events (promotions, maintenance) in the horizon visualization
acceptance_criteria: Clickable Figma prototype that simulates timeline adjustments and shows updated cost/SLO delta
Design spec with component-level tokens, states, and transition behavior (hover/focus/drag) uploaded to the design library
Operator usability test: at least 5 participants from SRE/platform with median time-to-complete < 90s for a standard burst change scenario
Handoff package including annotated copy, accessibility notes, and payload shape for preview API
Design review approval (thumbs-up) from PM and two ENG reviewers recorded in comments
